Supplementary Information

Title: Utilizing Nanoinducers for Precision Degradation of Bacterial

             Protein to Mitigate Antibiotic Resistance

Supplementary Figure 1. Molecular docking analysis was performed to investigate
the interactions of pMurD with MurD and tSsrA with SspB in S. aureus. a, Close-
up views and electrostatic surface representations of the pMurD binding to the major
pocket in MurD. MurD and pMurD are depicted in gray and color, respectively. A
magnified view of the interaction of MurD with pMurD is shown in the dashed box.
Amino acids involved in the hydrogen bond formation are connected with green dashed
lines. b, Close-up views and the electrostatic surface representations of the tSsrA
binding to the major pocket in SspB. SspB and tSsrA are depicted in gray and color,
respectively. A magnified view of the interaction of SspB with tSsrA is shown in the
dashed box. Amino acids involved in the hydrogen bond formation are connected with
green dashed lines.

Supplementary Figure 2. OD600 of planktonic growth suspension of S. aureus and
S. typhimurium. Bacteria were incubated with bacNIDs with indicated feeding ratio at
a concentration of 100 μM. Data were presented as mean ± s.d. (n = 3 biologically
independent samples). Source data are provided as a Source Data file.

Supplementary Figure 3. characterization of bacNIDs. a, HPLC profiles of pMurD
and tSsrA before and after conjugation on GNPs. b, The UV-vis absorption spectra of
GNPs and bacNIDs showed similar absorption peak. c, Zeta potential of GNPs, M-
GNPs, S-GNPs, and bacNIDs determined by DLS at room temperature. Data were
presented as mean ± s.d. (n = 3 independent samples). d, TEM images and size
distribution of M-GNPs and S-GNPs. The experiment was performed twice with similar
results. Source data are provided in the Source Data file.

Supplementary Figure 4. TEM images of unstained superthin slices of S. aureus
and S. typhimurium with internalized GNPs or bacNIDs.

Supplementary Figure 5. Immunoblot of MurA, MurE, MurG, and MurD in S.
aureus and S. typhimurium treated with bacNIDs at indicated concentrations for
12 h. The experiment was performed twice with similar results. Source data are
provided in the Source Data file.

Supplementary Figure 6. Immunoblot of MurD in Gram-positive bacteria (S.
aureus, MRSA, S. epidermidis) and the Gram-negative bacterium (S. typhimurium,
E. coli, P. aeruginosa). The experiment was performed twice with similar results.
Source data are provided in the Source Data file.

Supplementary Figure 7. Relative optical density (OD600) of planktonic growth
suspension of S. aureus and S. typhimurium after 12 h of incubation under the
indicated treatments. Data were presented as mean ± s.d. (n = 3 biologically
independent samples). Source data are provided in the Source Data file.

Supplementary Figure 8. Time-kill curves of norfloxacin and bacNIDs against S.
aureus and S. typhimurium. Data were presented as mean ± s.d. (n = 3 biologically
independent samples). Source data are provided in the Source Data file.

Supplementary Figure 9. The relative optical density (OD600) of planktonic
growth suspension of S. aureus and S. typhimurium after 12 h of incubation under
the indicated treatments and nutrient-limited conditions. Data were presented as
mean ± s.d. (n = 3 biologically independent samples). Source data are provided in the
Source Data file.

Supplementary Figure 10. The relative optical density (OD600) of planktonic
cultures and western blot analysis of MurD in persister cells of S. aureus and S.
typhimurium after 12 h of incubation with the specified treatment. Data were
presented as mean ± s.d. (n = 3 biologically independent samples). Western blotting
was performed twice, with similar results. Source data are provided in the Source Data
file.

Supplementary Figure 11. The relative optical density (OD600) of planktonic
cultures and western blot analysis of MurD of S. epidermidis (a) and P. aeruginosa
(b) after 12 hours of incubation with the specified treatment. Data were presented
as mean ± s.d. (n = 3 biologically independent samples). Western blotting was
performed twice, with similar results. Source data are provided in the Source Data file.

Supplementary Figure 12. Immunoblot analysis of MurD levels and measurement
of the relative optical density (OD600) of planktonic cultures of (a) S. aureus
treated with bacNIDs and hinokiflavone (100 μM), and (b) S. typhimurium treated
with bacNIDs and (3R, 4R)-A2-32-01 (50 μM) for 12 h. Data are presented as mean
± s.d. (n = 3 biologically independent samples). The experiment was performed twice
with similar results. Source data are provided in the Source Data file.

Supplementary Figure 13. Immunoblot analysis of MurD levels and measurement
of the optical density (OD600) of planktonic cultures of S. aureus and S.
typhimurium treated with bacNIDs with key residue mutations. Data are presented
as mean ± s.d. (n = 3 biologically independent samples). Western blotting was
performed twice, with similar results. Source data are provided in the Source Data file.

Supplementary Figure 14. Cytotoxicity of bacNIDs on eukaryotic cells. a, Cell
viability of NIH/3T3, (b) HUVECs, and (c) RAW 264.7 cells after treated with bacNIDs
at indicated concentrations. Data were presented as mean ± s.d. (n = 3 biologically
independent samples). Source data are provided in the Source Data file.

Supplementary Figure 15. The relative optical density (OD600) of planktonic
growth suspension of Bifidobacterium and A. muciniphila after 12 h of incubation
under the indicated treatments. Data were presented as mean ± s.d. (n = 3 biologically
independent samples). Source data are provided in the Source Data file.

Supplementary Figure 16. OD600 of planktonic growth suspension of S. aureus
and S. typhimurium treated with bacNIDs after incubation in 10% FBS, simulated
body fluid, or simulated intestinal fluid. Data were presented as mean ± s.d. (n = 3
biologically independent samples). Source data are provided in the Source Data file.

Supplementary Figure 17. Antibacterial activity of Pt-bacNIDs. a, TEM images and
zeta potentials of Pt NPs and Pt-bacNIDs. Scale bars, 20 nm. The data are presented as
the mean ± s.d. (n = 3 independent samples). b, Photographs of colony formation and
immunoblotting data of MurD expression of S. aureus after Pt NPs or Pt-bacNIDs
treatments. c, Photographs of colony formation and immunoblotting data of MurD
expression of S. typhimurium after Pt NPs or Pt-bacNIDs treatments. The experiment
was performed twice with similar results. Source data are provided in the Source Data
file.

Supplementary Figure 18. Antibacterial activity of Pd-bacNIDs. a, TEM images
and zeta potentials of Pd NPs and Pd-bacNIDs. Scale bars, 20 nm. The data are
presented as the mean ± s.d. (n = 3 independent samples). b, Photographs of colony
formation and immunoblotting data of MurD expression of S. aureus after Pd NPs or
Pd-bacNIDs treatments. c, Photographs of colony formation and immunoblotting data
of MurD expression of S. typhimurium after Pd NPs or Pd-bacNIDs treatments. The
experiment was performed twice with similar results. Source data are provided in the
Source Data file.

Supplementary Figure 19. Quantitative analysis of PI fluorescence intensity in
bacteria. a, PI fluorescence intensity of S. aureus and (b) S. typhimurium after PBS,
GNPs, M-GNPs, S-GNPs, or bacNIDs. Data were presented as mean ± s.d. (n = 3
biologically independent samples). One-way ANOVA with Tukey's multiple
comparisons was used to calculate statistical differences. Source data are provided in
the Source Data file.

Supplementary Figure 20. AKP activity of S. aureus and S. typhimurium after
bacNIDs treatment at the indicated concentrations. The data are presented as the
mean ± s.d. (n = 3 biologically independent samples). One-way ANOVA with Tukey's
multiple comparisons was used to calculate statistical differences. Source data are
provided in the Source Data file.

Supplementary Figure 21. OD600 of planktonic growth suspension of S. aureus
and S. typhimurium after treatment with norfloxacin at the indicated
concentrations. Data were presented as mean ± s.d. (n = 3 biologically independent
samples). Source data are provided in the Source Data file.

Supplementary Figure 22. Generation of norfloxacin-resistant mutations in S.
aureus. Antibacterial activity of planktonic growth suspension after 12 h of incubation
with norfloxacin. Data were presented as mean ± s.d. (n = 3 biologically independent
samples). Source data are provided in the Source Data file.

Supplementary Figure 23. Generation of norfloxacin-resistant mutations in S.
typhimurium. Antibacterial activity of planktonic growth suspension after 12 h of
incubation with norfloxacin. Data were presented as mean ± s.d. (n = 3 biologically
independent samples). Source data are provided in the Source Data file.

Supplementary Figure 24. The killing effect of bacNIDs on different drug-resistant
bacteria. a, Antimicrobial resistance testing of norfloxacin against S. epidemidis and P.
aeruginosa. The relative optical density (OD600) of planktonic cultures and western
blot analysis of MurD of S. epidermidis-9 (b) and P. aeruginosa-9 (c) after 12 hours of
incubation with the specified treatment. Data were presented as mean ± s.d. (n = 3
biologically independent samples). Western blotting was performed twice, with similar
results. Source data are provided in the Source Data file.

Supplementary Figure 25. Antimicrobial resistance testing of bacNIDs and
imipenem against S. aureus and S. typhimurium. Source data are provided in the
Source Data file.

Supplementary Figure 26. Body weight of the mice with S. aureus-infected skin
wounds after various treatments. Data were presented as mean ± s.d. (n = 5 mice per
group). Source data are provided in the Source Data file.

Supplementary Figure 27. In vivo biodistribution of bacNIDs after topical
application to wound sites. a, IVIS imaging of excisional wound mice treated with
Cy5.5-labelled bacNIDs. b, Quantitative analysis of Cy5.5 fluorescence intensity in
wound sites treated with bacNIDs. The data are presented as the mean ± s.d. (n = 3 mice
per group). c, The contents of bacNIDs in major organs, eschar, and blood were
measured by ICP-MS in an excisional wound mouse model. The data are presented as
the mean ± s.d. (n = 3 mice per group). Source data are provided in the Source Data file.

Supplementary Figure 28. Quantification of collagen deposition in S. aureus-
infected nonhealing skin wounds after various treatments. Data were presented as
mean ± s.d. (n = 3 mice per group). Source data are provided in the Source Data file.

Supplementary Figure 29. Body weight of the mice with S. aureus-infected
nonhealing skin wounds after various treatments. Data were presented as mean ±
s.d. (n = 5 mice per group). Source data are provided in the Source Data file.

Supplementary Figure 30. In vivo safety assessment of bacNIDs. a, Body weight of
db/db mice with S. aureus-infected keratitis after various treatments. Data were
presented as mean ± s.d. (n = 5 mice per group). b, H&E images of major organs
collected from db/db mice after indicated treatment on day 20. Scale bars, 100 μm. Data
are representative of three biologically independent experiments. Source data are
provided in the Source Data file.

Supplementary Figure 31. Hematological examination of db/db mice after
indicated treatment on day 20. WBC, white blood cells; RBC, red blood cells; HGB,
hemoglobin; HCT, hematocrit; MCV, mean cell volume; MCH, mean corpuscular
hemoglobin; MPV, mean platelet volume; RDW, red cell distribution width; HDW,
hemoglobin distribution width; PLT, blood platelet. Data were presented as mean ± s.d.
(n = 3 mice per group). Source data are provided in the Source Data file.

Supplementary Figure 32. In vivo anti-infectious efficacy of bacNIDs in S.
typhimurium-induced colitis model. a, Survival rates of mice in the indicated
treatment groups. b, Body weights of mice after their respective treatments. Data were
presented as mean ± s.d. (n = 10 mice per group). c, Representative macroscopic images
of colon morphology from the treated mice. d, Average colon length. e, Histological
analysis of the colon by H&E staining (×20 magnification; scale bar, 100 μm). Data are
representative of three biologically independent experiments. One-way ANOVA with
Tukey's multiple comparisons was used to calculate statistical differences. Source data
are provided in the Source Data file.

Supplementary Figure 33. Effects of the indicated treatments on serum levels of
IL-6 and TNF-α in mice. Data were presented as mean ± s.d. (n = 3 mice per group).
Source data are provided in the Source Data file.

Supplementary Figure 34. Biosafety assessment of bacNIDs. a, Hematological
analysis of mice treated with bacNIDs. Data are shown as the mean ± s.d. (n =3 mice
per group). b, ALT, CK, CREA and UREA in serum from mice after treatment with
bacNIDs. Data are shown as the mean ± s.d. (n =3 mice per group). Source data are
provided in the Source Data file.
